claims.text: Bulbapedia says Premium File 2 was first available at participating cinemas showing Spell of the Unown: Entei from July 8, 2000, with general release following on August 5, 2000; this supersedes the local source row's inherited continuation-slice date baggage for product-route discussion.
Bulbapedia's Neo TCG Era merchandise page says Premium File 2 was released as an accompaniment with the second Neo era expansion Crossing the Ruins... and includes nine special cards.

Bulbapedia's Charizard page says this card was one of nine Unnumbered Promotional cards in Premium File 2, initially sold at participating cinemas showing Spell of the Unown: Entei from July 8, 2000 and generally released on August 5, 2000.

The local source slice models one source-pinned Charizard row for this route: source index 184; a separate existing source-set models the adjacent eight-row Premium File 2 group at source indices 185-192.

Bulbapedia's Neo TCG Era merchandise page says all Premium File 2 cards feature a Cosmos Reverse Holofoil treatment, and that Charizard, Entei, and Pichu have ties to Spell of the Unown: Entei / Pikachu & Pichu.
Bulbapedia credits the Charizard (Premium File 2 promo) illustration to Ken Sugimori / 杉森建.

Bulbapedia's Sugimori profile identifies him as the illustrator of the original artwork for the Pokemon games and the original artwork for all 151 Generation I Pokemon, making his Charizard credit part of the official visual grammar collectors recognize across routes.

Bulbapedia lists this Charizard as LV.78, Fire type, Stage 2, HP 120, No. 006, with the Pokemon Power Fire Raise and the attack Fire Spin for 100; its Fire Spin effect matches Base Set Charizard while the card route remains Premium File 2.

Agents should keep source row 184 separate from the adjacent local Premium File 2 eight-row group, Base Set Charizard, Japanese Expansion Pack / No Rarity Charizard, Song Best Charizard, Trade Please Charizard, English jumbo Charizard, Base Set 2, Legendary Collection, Celebrations, and modern classic reprints.

The catalog can make the Premium File 2 Charizard route, movie/cinema context, reverse-holo surface, and source-index boundary legible, but it does not prove seller possession, authenticity, condition, price, sealed-file completeness, or spendability.

narrative.human_title: Premium File 2 Charizard — the fire that refuses to be just Base Set again
narrative.why_it_matters: This is a perfect Charizard trap. The name is loud enough to drown out the route, and the Fire Spin echo tempts a lazy agent back toward Base Set memory. But row 184 is its own assembly: a Neo-era Premium File 2 object, tied to Spell of the Unown cinema distribution, wrapped in Cosmos reverse holofoil, and standing just beside an eight-row Premium File 2 group without becoming the same catalog family. The awe is real; the shortcut is not.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat source row 184 as the Premium File 2 Charizard singleton with cinema/movie route and reverse-holo surface, not as Base Set Charizard or the adjacent eight-row Premium File 2 group.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller note, or agent memory says Charizard, リザードン, Lizardon, Premium File 2, Neo Premium File 2, Spell of the Unown, Entei movie, Cosmos reverse holo, Fire Raise, Fire Spin, No. 006, or source index 184.
steps: Anchor the route to Premium File 2 / プレミアムファイル2, with first cinema availability from July 8, 2000 and general release on August 5, 2000.
Confirm the candidate is Charizard / リザードン / Lizardon, LV.78, Fire type, Stage 2, HP 120, No. 006, not another Charizard surface.
Preserve source index 184 as a singleton local catalog route; do not absorb it into the adjacent eight-row Premium File 2 source group at rows 185-192.
Look for Cosmos Reverse Holofoil / Premium File 2 surface context when seller photos allow; do not infer the surface from name alone.
Use Ken Sugimori / 杉森建 as the expected artist credit.
Treat Fire Raise and Fire Spin as useful row details; do not let Fire Spin collapse this into Base Set Charizard or No Rarity Charizard.
Separate this row from Song Best Charizard, Trade Please Charizard, English jumbo Charizard, Base Set 2, Legendary Collection, Celebrations, metal cards, and modern classic reprints.
If a seller offers a complete Premium File 2, ask whether Charizard is present, attached, removed, substituted, or separately photographed; file possession is not card possession.
Before any funded trade, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card or exact sealed/file state being claimed.

card_highlights.why_it_matters: Charizard usually arrives with thunder. Here the interesting part is restraint: the agent has to honor the Charizard gravity while keeping it pinned to Premium File 2, movie distribution, reverse-holo surface, and row 184. Same monster. Different apparatus.

narrative.why_it_matters: The joy of this card is that it looks easy and is not. Charizard, Sugimori, Fire Spin: the brain races to Base Set. But the right collector read is more specific and more interesting. This is a Premium File 2 object, tied to a Neo movie moment, with a reverse-holo treatment and a source-index boundary that keeps it from becoming just another famous dragon in a price search.
